continuity_scope: Sword Art Online 1: Aincrad, Yen On English light novel, author Reki Kawahara, translated Stephen Paul, 22 April 2014, ISBN 9780316371247, 264 pages, Teen. Excludes web novel, manga, anime, films, games, later arcs/volumes, guides, and adaptations.
coverage_rule: Terms-only pass. The exact Vol. 1 publisher synopsis names no individual character, so it cannot support a Kirito/avatar/real-name record or a relationship. Player roles, guilds, skills, items, Aincrad, VR systems, and death-game rules remain terms.
omissions: All named people, including avatar/real-world identities, because none is named in selected Vol. 1 synopsis.
All later arcs, web novel, manga, anime, films, games, guides, and adaptations.
Player roles, guilds, skills, items, Aincrad, NerveGear, systems, and themes as character endpoints.
content_cautions: The official premise concerns captivity, inability to log out, bodily confinement, and certain real-and-virtual death on game over; it can be distressing.
No detailed coercion/violence scene is reconstructed from metadata.
uncertainties: No page-addressable prose locator was accessible, so real/player avatar identity claims are omitted.
evidence_basis: Yen Press establishes edition, translation, VR death-game and Aincrad premise; separate Re:Aincrad product establishes adaptation boundary. No unofficial or adaptation character claims used.
